title: Taiwan's Tourism Administration: 12 travel agencies reported personal-data leaks in 3 years
date_note: Date of the Liberty Times and Knews articles reporting the Tourism Administration's figures; neither gives an earlier day for the statement.
org: Taiwan travel agencies (Tourism Administration, Ministry of Transportation and Communications)
geo_basis: Taiwan's Tourism Administration as the source of the statistics; agencies named are in Taiwan
summary: Taiwan's Tourism Administration says 12 travel agencies reported personal-data leaks over the past 3 years, with about 1.55 million records leaked in total and fines of NT$3.65 million. Reports rose from 1 in 2024 to 3 in 2025 and 8 so far in 2026. Yi You Net reported an external attack on its member centre on 7 November, with over 690,000 people affected.
plain: Taiwan's tourism regulator says travel-company data leaks are rising: 12 firms reported leaks in 3 years, about 1.55 million records, including Yi You Net's over 690,000 people affected.
exec: Travel firms hold passport and itinerary data; the regulator reports rising leak reports and fines of NT$3.65 million.
action: General advice: customers of Taiwanese travel agencies should be wary of messages that use their booking details and confirm them with the agency directly.
impact: About 1.55 million records leaked across 12 agencies in 3 years, per the Tourism Administration.

evidence.quote: 交通部觀光署統計，旅行業通報個資外洩案逐年增加，近3年共有12家，外洩個資累積約155萬筆
該署已依法裁處罰鍰共365萬元

validation.note: Liberty Times and Knews both relay the Tourism Administration's statistics (shared sourcing), so treated as one source; the Administration's own statement was not read.
